investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable — no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~141–145 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval runner timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable — no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~141–145 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval runner timed out, producing zero evidence and a full contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the 2 kata/peerpods-capable nodes are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes qualify for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and those 2 nodes are at capacity; the other 4 nodes are excluded by affinity/selector rules, leaving no scheduling path.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for remote-agent workloads: the total number of kata.peerpods.io/vm slots across the cluster is insufficient to handle concurrent eval probes plus any live remote-agent workloads running at the same time.

Lower confidence — a recent node drain, node failure, or resource quota change reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity below the minimum needed for scheduling; no node event or quota evidence is present in the supplied packet to confirm this.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io VM pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected by any check, and the contract-required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are entirely absent because agent creation never completed.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval's remote agent pod: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~141–145 seconds across all three checks, no agent was ever created, no VM became ready, and no runtime response was produced. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.
